description: A live, local view of Retsu accepting, prioritising, delivering, retrying, expiring, and cleaning messages under the showcase workload.

panels.description: Messages accepted by Retsu each second for the active showcase run.
panels.title: Accepted messages

panels.description: Successful application requests as a percentage of all showcase API requests. The local objective is at least 99.99%.
panels.title: Availability

panels.description: Age of the oldest ready showcase message. Green is comfortably within the 10-second visibility objective.
panels.title: Oldest ready message

panels.description: The deliberately changing producer pulse against real message deliveries. The shape should move throughout the showcase.
panels.title: Showcase pulse

panels.description: Server-recorded enqueue and acknowledgement rates for showcase queues.
panels.title: Message flow

panels.description: Client-observed request rates by message operation, excluding setup and verification traffic.
panels.title: API operations

panels.description: Share of successfully enqueued showcase messages across the two hot, two warm, and one fault queue.
panels.title: Queue share

panels.description: The intended 70% high, 20% medium, and 10% low priority mix, measured from accepted messages.
panels.title: Priority mix

panels.description: Current ready and in-flight messages by priority across the selected showcase queues.
panels.title: Queue pressure

panels.description: Normal acknowledgements alongside the deliberate no-ack, expiry, and dead-letter paths exercised by the showcase.
panels.title: Message outcomes

panels.description: First, second, and third delivery attempts. Later-attempt activity makes retries visible without counting them as failures.
panels.title: Delivery attempts

panels.description: Cleaner passes stay visible even when there is nothing to remove. Expired messages are cleaned during the showcase; DLQ purge appears after the one-hour local retention.
panels.title: Cleaner activity

panels.description: Server-side latency across queue API routes. Exemplars link latency spikes to Tempo traces when available.
panels.title: API latency

panels.description: The deliberate 1s, 2s, 3s, and 5s consumer work mix as observed by k6.
panels.title: Consumer processing time

panels.description: Oldest ready and in-flight message age by priority. The dashed threshold marks ten seconds.
panels.title: Message age

panels.description: CPU cores used by the services doing the work. One means one fully occupied CPU core.
panels.title: CPU usage

panels.description: Working-set memory for the application and its data path, excluding monitoring tools.
panels.title: Memory working set

panels.description: Accepted plus acknowledged messages divided by CPU cores consumed by the application and data path. Higher means more work from the same laptop budget.
panels.title: Work per CPU core

panels.description: Application-side SQLx connections in use as a percentage of each component's configured maximum.
panels.title: Application pool utilisation

panels.description: Active and total PostgreSQL sessions against the configured server maximum.
panels.title: PostgreSQL sessions

panels.description: PgBouncer client demand and backend usage. Waiting clients should remain at zero during a healthy showcase.
panels.title: PgBouncer pressure

panels.description: Queue-name lookup cache hit ratio. A warm cache should remain high.
panels.title: Cache hit ratio

panels.description: Cache hits and misses served by the local in-memory and Dragonfly-backed lookup path.
panels.title: Cache requests

panels.description: Time spent loading a queue name when it is not already cached.
panels.title: Cache load latency

panels.description: Scrape health for the Retsu processes and their essential local dependencies.
panels.title: Component health

panels.description: Age and success of the queue-state snapshot that powers depth and oldest-age panels.
panels.title: Queue-state telemetry

panels.description: CPU throttling and memory-limit usage for the application and data path. Any OOM event is shown in the legend.
panels.title: Resource pressure

list.description: Showcase queue name. Leave this on all queues for the full product story.
list.label: Queue
list.name: queue
